messages.body_plain:
Ed

I was trying to use the monitor argument in the jagextra to export the factor scores (eta) from a simple model, when I try to include it I get an error and the model doesnt even does the estimation. Is there a good way to estract the posterior draws for the factors?

Thanks

################################################################################
mod51 <- 'Positive =~ great + cheerful + happy
          Negative =~ sad + down + unhappy
'
fit51 <-  bcfa(mod51, data=dat, std.lv <http://std.lv>=T,
n.chains = 3, burnin=5000,
            sample=2000, jagfile="cfa1",
jagextra = list(monitor="eta"))

Error:
Error in lavjags$summaries[xlocs, "Mean"] : invalid subscript type 'list'

> >
> > Ed
> >
> >

> > On Mon, Dec 19, 2016 at 11:42 AM, Andy Field <an...@sussex.ac.uk> wrote:
> > > Hi Ed,

> > > Can I pick up on this and ask for a bit more detail (or some references to follow up)? I'm being asked to explain why I haven't used multiple imputation in a growth model with blavaan. I'm fairly new to Bayes so apologies if my terminology/phrasing is sloppy. My understanding is that if you use MCMC then missing values are estimated by drawing expected values from the initial posterior distributions for parameter estimates of the model. These 'expected' missing values would in turn inform the next iteration of posteriors, which in turn would update the 'expected' missing values and so on until the iterations are complete. messages.body_plain:
Luis

The error of the summary function may be related to a bug that is fix in the development version, try to explicitly set the burnin and sample, like
bsem(total, data = subjcharac, adapt=1000, burnin=5000, sample=4000)

The ppp is (for now) the only measure of absolute fit, BUT is not reliable, it is very easy for it to find a model to have bad fit. Think of it similar to the p-value of the chisquare in the frequentist SEM. For now I would recommend you to look at the fit in function of the parameters, are the standardized factor loadings large, factor correlation make theoretical sense, etc

About missing data, blvaan does handle missing data , it handles it as JAGS handles missing data as default. With data augmentation, at each iteration values are imputed into the missing values, the imputations are drawn from the posterior distribution conditional on the model parameters. So, missing values are both parameters and data

Hope this helps
